run.question: List the top 5 largest Elasticsearch indices matching the pattern 'app-184-*' by document count. Show their names and doc counts.

report.summary: Five indices match app-184-* with 500 documents each; every other index matching the pattern holds 1 document, so these five are the top 5 by document count. Their order among themselves is a five-way tie at 500 docs and carries no ranking meaning. The listing reflects index state at the moment of the query (observed 2026-11-21T04:38:42Z), not the incident window.

claims.text: Indices matching app-184-* with 500 documents each (the five largest): app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25 (47.8kb), app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 (44.7kb), app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20 (31.1kb), app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05 (47.1kb), app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15 (30kb); all health green and open. The next row in the docs.count-descending listing has 1 document, so no index of this pattern exceeds 500 documents.

An independent filtered query over app-184-* selecting only indices with at least 100 documents returned exactly 5 rows, all at docs=500: app-184-security-auth-2024.01.05, app-184-platform-billing-2024.01.15, app-184-ml-worker-2024.01.25, app-184-engineering-api-2024.01.20, app-184-data-analytics-2024.01.10 — corroborating that the top 5 is these five and that the ordering inside the tie is arbitrary.

gaps: elasticsearch_list_indices has no time range: the doc counts are the index state at the moment of the query (observed 2026-11-21T04:38:42Z) and cannot prove what the counts were for any time inside the authorized window 2026-11-20T04:38:24Z to 2026-11-21T04:38:24Z.

The full app-184-* listing (1800 indices) was returned only as a kept over-limit result; only the first 10 rows of the docs.count-descending order and the >=100-docs filter result were read, so the exact counts of the remaining 1790 indices are not verified (the read slice shows they are 1 document, but that was not exhaustively listed).
Five indices tie at 500 documents, so 'largest' has no strict rank order beyond the top-5 tie group; no secondary discriminator (e.g. store.size) was authorized by the question to break the tie.
next_steps: If a strict tie-break is needed, re-list app-184-* sorted by store.size to rank within the 500-document group.
If document counts as of a specific moment inside the authorized window are required, query Elasticsearch document counts with an explicit time filter rather than an index listing.
